Used double-glazed glass production machinery is now widely used in the manufacture of double-glazed windows. An important consideration is that the finished windows must provide effective thermal and acoustic insulation. The performance of the window depends significantly on the double-glazed unit installed in it.
Over the past few decades, the double-glazing industry has expanded considerably, with many companies in Iran and around the world active in manufacturing this high-demand product.
In this article, we discuss the double-glazing industry and introduce the essential machinery required for producing different types of insulated glass units.

settings.title: Everything You Need to Know About Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
Concerns about dwindling natural resources and non-renewable energy have grown considerably over recent centuries. One of humanity's most fundamental challenges is how to use energy efficiently.
For this reason, various methods are now used to prevent energy waste in different sectors.
Since buildings and construction account for a significant share of energy losses, double-glazed glass is widely used in buildings.
In fact, installing this type of glass is one of the most effective ways to improve energy efficiency in buildings.
The main features and benefits of double-glazed glass include:
• It provides excellent sound insulation, significantly reducing noise from busy streets and outdoor areas entering the building.
• With double-glazed windows, a building's heating and cooling systems consume less energy, making this glass an important part of energy efficiency.
• Double-glazed glass offers greater safety than ordinary glass. If cracked by impact or pressure, the panes are less likely to collapse and remain held in place.
• Double-glazed glass can help control the amount of incoming light and reduce the penetration of harmful solar radiation.
• Because the temperature of the inner pane is largely influenced by the indoor environment rather than outdoor conditions, condensation on the glass surface is minimized.

settings.title: The Double-Glazed Glass Production Process
settings.text:
In general, the production of double- and triple-glazed glass involves joining glass panes in parallel, creating an insulating space between the layers.
The aim is to form a sealed cavity filled with dry air or a gas that improves the unit's insulating properties.
A closer look at the production process shows that the glass is first cut to the required dimensions and thickness.
An aluminium-alloy spacer is then used to maintain the gap between the two panes.
The spacer is filled with a moisture-absorbing material, such as silica gel, to remove moisture from the space between the panes and keep the cavity dry.
At a controlled temperature, a special adhesive called butyl is applied to the spacer, which is then joined to the glass panes. Polysulfide sealant is also used to seal the edges around the spacer and glass.
Argon, a dry, inert, odourless gas, is injected between the panes to create an insulating cavity.

settings.title: Key Considerations Before Setting Up a Double-Glazed Glass Production Line
settings.text:
The many benefits of double-glazed glass discussed above have encouraged more consumers to choose this type of glazing.
As a result, setting up a double-glazed glass production line has become an attractive idea for many entrepreneurs and industry professionals.
Double-glazed glass must be manufactured in accordance with specific standards. These standards are based on requirements from industrialized countries and the Iranian National Standards Organization, and are communicated to manufacturing facilities.
Anyone planning to establish a double-glazed glass production line should first pay close attention to the following standards and factors:
1. Thickness of the double-glazed unit
2. Dimensions of the unit (length and width)
3. Spacer thickness
4. Climatic conditions
5. Resistance to moisture
6. Frost formation
7. Fogging
Another important consideration in industrial double-glazing production is that all stages of the factory production line should be carried out using automated machinery.
